habitat: Mixed grass and bushveld, forest fringes, coastal scrub and old cultivated lands. Flocks clamber on grass stems.
summary: A very common resident. Earth-brown upper parts grade to blackish on the head, face, throat and upper breast. Those blackish areas are washed bottle-green or bronze, and some bottle-green feathers sit on the mantle. The underparts are white, the flanks are finely barred, and the upper mandible is dark. The immature has an all-dark bill and upper parts less rufous than an immature Red-backed Mannikin. The call is a wheezy chik, chik, chikka. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Red-backed Mannikin is red-brown above, with more extensive black and broader flank bars, and a blue-grey bill.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^13=8192 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 4096–16384.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

upperparts.pattern: Less rufous than the immature Red-backed Mannikin.

viewNotes.note: Blackish head and breast with a bronze or bottle-green wash, earth-brown above and white below.
Blackish face, throat and upper breast. The upper mandible is dark.
Earth-brown upper parts, with some bottle-green feathers on the mantle.
When flushed, the flock flies into a bush. A wing pattern was not described.
White underparts and finely barred flanks.

calls.description: A wheezy chik, chik, chikka. Grade A call from Kirstenbosch. The filename is generic and shows a 250 Hz high-pass. It was not cleaned again.
